judgment_notes: Razborov, Flag algebras (2007). Many commits carry AI trailers.

source.citation: A. A. Razborov, Flag algebras, Journal of Symbolic Logic 72(4) (2007) 1239-1282
source.scope: core theory (flags, flag algebra, unlabeling operator, limit objects / random homomorphisms, positivity, Cauchy-Schwarz) plus Mantel's theorem as an application
source.evidence: README: "The goal of this project is to formalize the results of the paper Flag Algebras (https://people.cs.uchicago.edu/~razborov/files/flag.pdf) by Alexander A. Razborov"; blueprint "maps the core of the LeanFlagAlgebras library", organised by library modules, no section references. Paper is 44 pp.; ~25 pp. for Sections 2-3 core.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Unlabel: $\mathrm{unlabel}$ drops the type embedding of a single flag, returning its underlying graph as an unlabeled ($\emptyset$-type) flag.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma Expected density is the downward ratio: The expected $F$-density under a large flag's measure equals the normalized downward density ratio; the finite-level identity behind Lemma~3.11.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Edge and triangle densities: $K_2, K_3 \in \mathcal{A}^\emptyset$ are the edge- and triangle-density basis elements. For a positive homomorphism $\varphi$, $\varphi(K_2)$ is the edge density and $\varphi(K_3)$ the triangle density.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem Mantel, flag-algebra form: In $\mathcal{A}^\emptyset$, $K_2 \le \tfrac12\cdot 1 + K_3$.

edge_sample.source_text: theorem Defining property of $\mathbb{P}[\varphi_0]$: Integrating $\varphi \mapsto \varphi(f)$ against $\mathbb{P}[\varphi_0]$ recovers $\varphi_0[\![f]\!]_0 / \varphi_0[\![1]\!]_0$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : Apply the $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz (Hölder) inequality to the evaluation functions $\varphi \mapsto \varphi(f), \varphi(g)$ under $\mathbb{P}[\varphi_0]$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:prob-measure-spec}), handling the degenerate base case with Lemma~\ref{

edge_sample.source_text: lemma Complete-bipartite lower bound: For $n \ge 2$, the maximal edge density of a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices is at least $\tfrac12$, witnessed by the balanced complete bipartite graph: $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_3)/\binom{n}{2} \ge \tfrac12$.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem Tur\'an density of the triangle: $\pi(K_3) = \tfrac12$.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Downward operator: $[\![\,\cdot\,]\!]_0 : \mathcal{A}^\sigma \to \mathcal{A}^\emptyset$ is the $\mathbb{R}$-linear map induced by $F \mapsto w(F)\cdot \mathrm{unlabel}\,F$; it averages a labeled element over all unlabelings.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem Squares have nonnegative average: $[\![f\cdot f]\!]_0 \ge 0$ for every $f$: the downward image of a square is nonnegative.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma Order arithmetic: The semantic order is compatible with the algebra operations: inequalities may be added termwise, and a nonnegative scalar times a nonnegative element is nonnegative.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma Translation invariance of the order: Adding a fixed element on either side preserves the semantic order; these register as the \texttt{AddLeftMono}/\texttt{AddRightMono} instances.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma Limit measure is supported on homomorphisms: The weak limit of a convergent flag sequence's probability measures is concentrated on the positive-homomorphism space.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem Random homomorphism measure (Razborov 3.5): For a base homomorphism $\varphi_0$ on the empty type with $\varphi_0\langle\sigma\rangle_0 > 0$, there is a probability measure $\mathbb{P}[\varphi_0]$ on the positive-homomorphism space whose expectation recovers the normalized downward o

edge_sample.source_text: definition Positive homomorphism: A \emph{positive homomorphism} is an $\mathbb{R}$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi : \mathcal{A}^\sigma \to \mathbb{R}$ that is nonnegative on every flag. These are the semantic evaluations of the algebra --- the limits of subgraph densities.
edge_sample.target_text: definition Semantic cone: The \emph{semantic cone} is $\{\, f \mid \varphi(f) \ge 0 \text{ for all positive } \varphi \,\}$. Membership is exactly an unconditional density inequality.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Single, pair, and triple densities: The fixed-arity specializations $d_1(F;G)$, $d_2(F_1,F_2;G)$, $d_3(F_1,F_2,F_3;G)$ are list densities of the singleton, pair, and triple lists. $d_2$ is the factor multiplication is built from; $d_1$ is the ordinary subflag density.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem Counting identity: Equating the three counts yields \[ d_1(\mathrm{unlabel}\,F;\,F')\cdot w(F) \;=\; \sum_{G \in \mathrm{ext}(F')} d_1(F;G)\cdot w(G), \] where $w$ is the normalizing factor and $\mathrm{ext}(F')$ ranges over the relabellings of $F'$. This is

edge_sample.source_text: definition Basis vector: $\mathrm{basisVector}\,F$ is the unit vector supported on the single flag $F$; every construction reduces to these.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem Nontriviality: $0 \ne 1$ in $\mathcal{A}^\sigma$: the flag algebra is nontrivial (so its $\mathrm{CommRing}$ structure is not the zero ring).
